user: one of the causes of the german hyperinflationary period that occurred after world war i was
assistant: The German hyper-inflationary period that occurred after World War I was caused by several factors, one of which was the heavy tribute that Germany had to pay in the form of war reparation. The Weimar Republic printed trillions of marks , causing extremely high inflation of the German currency. The burden became unbearable after the Great Depression. Nonetheless , even the payment of this small percentage of the original reparations ( 132 billion gold marks ) still placed a significant burden on the German economy . Although the causes of the devastating post-war hyperinflation are complex and disputed , Germans blamed the near - collapse of their economy on the Treaty of Versailles, and some economists estimated that the reparations accounted for as much as one - third of the hyper - inflation .

assistant: The First World War began in 1914 when a Serbian backed organization assassinated the heir of the Austro - Hungarian throne, no - one could stop the conflict and the First World War broke out . It lasted to the final Armistice in 1918 . The Allied Powers , led by the British Empire , France , Russia until March 1918 , Japan and the United States after 1917 , defeated the Central Powers , led by the German Empire , Austro - Hungarian Empire and the Ottoman Empire.It is also called as the Great War , or the War to End All Wars.More than 70 million military personnel , including 60 million Europeans , were mobilised in one of the largest wars in history . Over nine million combatants and seven million civilians died as a result of the war ( including the victims of a number of genocides ) , a casualty rate exacerbated by the belligerents ' technological and industrial sophistication , and the tactical stalemate caused by gruelling trench warfare . It was one of the deadliest conflicts in history , and paved the way for major political changes , including revolutions in many of the nations involved . Unresolved rivalries still extant at the end of the conflict contributed to the start of the Second World War only twenty - one years later .

Great Depression after World War I
[The End of Current Turn Question]

[The Start of Reference Answer]
The Great Depression started in the United States after a major fall in stock prices that began around September 4 , 1929 , and became worldwide news with the stock market crash of October 29 , 1929 ( known as Black Tuesday ) . . Between 1929 and 1932 , worldwide gross domestic product ( GDP ) fell by an estimated 15 % .It was also largely caused by the decision of most western nations after World War I to return to the gold standard at the pre-war gold price .  By 1931 , the world was reeling from the worst depression of recent memory , and the entire structure of reparations and war debts collapsed . 
[The End of Reference Answer]

[The Start of Assistant's Answer]
The Great Depression struck when European economies were still dealing with the aftermath of World War I.

- According to the gold standard theory, a major cause was most Western nations’ decision after the war to restore the gold standard at the pre-war gold price. This created deflationary monetary conditions that gradually weakened many European economies (page 1).
- The United Kingdom had not fully recovered from World War I when the Depression began. It was driven off the gold standard in 1931 (page 1).
- By 1931, the worldwide depression had brought about the collapse of the reparations and war-debt structure (page 1).
[The End of Assistant's Answer]

[The Start of Document]
Causes of the Great Depression
By 1931 , the world was reeling from the worst depression of recent memory , and the entire structure of reparations and war debts collapsed .

Great Depression
The World Depression broke at a time when the United Kingdom had still not fully recovered from the effects of the First World War more than a decade earlier . The country was driven off the gold standard in 1931 .

Causes of the Great Depression
According to the gold standard theory of the Depression , the Depression was largely caused by the decision of most western nations after World War I to return to the gold standard at the pre-war gold price . Monetary policy , according to this view , was thereby put into a deflationary setting that would over the next decade slowly grind away at the health of many European economies .
[The End of Document]
